# Writing a `product-module` page

Generated from `product-module`'s own template declarations. It states what this type requires;
the rules that apply to every page are in `wiki-authoring-spec.md` beside this file.

- **Lives at** `product/modules/<module>.md`
- **Authorship** `canonical` — human-authored only — no agent drafts this type for you
- **Freshness** stale after 180d
- **Template version** 1 — set `template-version: 1`

## Frontmatter

Required on this type beyond the base fields (`title`, `type`, `created`, `updated`, `owner`, `authorship`):

- `audience`
- `kind` — one of `application`, `library`, `area`, `shared`

The template also scaffolds `template-version`, `sources`, `related`, `depends-on`, `origination`, `confidence`, `platforms` — fill or empty each one; leaving a placeholder is an error.

`owner:` is fixed to `product` — do not change it.

## Placeholders to replace

{{TITLE}} {{DATE}} {{CONFIDENCE}} {{ORIGINATION}} {{AUDIENCE}} {{KIND}} {{PLATFORMS}}. Leaving one in place is an error (`unsubstituted-token`), and so is leaving a template example line (`template-example-line`).

The body also carries 1 placeholder written in angle brackets — `<what is unresolved>`. Each stands for content you write; replace every one, including in a row whose other cells you have already filled. Leaving one is an error (`unsubstituted-placeholder`).

## Where this type may link

This page lives in `product/` (layer 1).

You may link to `domain/` — and to other pages in `product/`.

You may not link to `design/`, `engineering/`, `operations/`, `gtm/`, `governance/`. Those sub-wikis cite this one, never the other way round; when you need to name something there, name it in prose instead of linking it.

## Sections

Keep every heading, in this order: `## Summary`, `## Target users`, `## Platform`, `## Navigation`, `## Features`, `## Entities`, `## Quality attributes`, `## Boundaries`, `## Open questions`.

**Table columns you may not drop:**

- `## Open questions` — `Question` | `Owner` | `Resume condition`

## What the audit checks on this page

Because of the declarations above: template-sections, section-order, table-columns. Every page is also checked for empty sections, heading restatement, callout types and code pointers. Run `/wiki-conformance-audit` to see the full list with its verdict.

## After you save

Two steps finish the page and neither is in the template:

- Commit the file under your own identity — authorship is a git fact, not a frontmatter one.
- Run `/wiki-reindex` so the page appears in its sub-wiki `index.md` and in `_derived/cited-by.md`. Until then it exists but nothing links to it.
